title: Set four M3 heat-set inserts flush in a printed robot bracket with a soldering iron, then put the iron back in its stand
instruction: Set the four inserts flush into the bracket with the soldering iron, then put the iron back in its stand.
context: Printed parts of robots (gripper fingers, joint housings, sensor brackets) take their screws in brass heat-set inserts, set with a soldering iron and an insert tip: insert on the hole, tip pressed in square, stop at flush. A robot building robots does this many times per part. The insert sinks only while the plastic round it is soft: light steady pressure for a few seconds, the iron square to the hole, stopping by feel at flush. Pushed hard it ends loose; leaning, crooked; past flush the hot shoulder marks the part. The tool is hot and goes back into a sloping holder tube.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Blue silicone soldering mat (2 mm, 20 x 16 cm) at (27, -14.5). On it, an orange PETG bracket 80 x 40 x 12 mm (STL and drawing in README: four 4.0 mm holes 7 mm deep, 56 x 20 mm apart), long side along y, centred at (28, -18). In each hole a brass CNC Kitchen M3 standard insert (M3 x 5.7 mm, 4.6 mm OD), dropped in, top about 4.5 mm proud. Hakko FX-888D station at 245 C (unit off the table), iron with an M3 heat-set tip (Hakko T18 fit, e.g. Adafruit 4239) resting tip down in its holder: weighted base clamped to the table, tube 30 mm inside, 9 cm long, sloping 50 degrees down away from the arms, closed end at (42, -27), 3 cm up. Arms in the ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time the iron's tip or barrel touched the robot (real trial: came within 2 cm, e-stop), or the iron was out of its stand and in no grip for 2 s, or at the end it is not resting in its stand, released. Otherwise per insert: 0.25 if its top is within 0.5 mm of the face (rule across it, 0.5 mm feeler gauge, calipers); 0.10 if seated but not flush (0.5 to 2.5 mm proud, or 0.5 to 1 mm sunk); 0 if higher, or crooked (sunk with the iron leaning over 5 degrees: a hand-threaded M3 x 12 screw stands over 1 mm off a try square), forced (pushed over 15 N while sinking: the insert turns when the screw is tightened), or next to a melt mark (hot iron on the face 0.5 s: photo). Success 1.0: all four flush, iron in its stand, 1 s.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo needs about 1,350
reset_notes: Each trial uses a fresh printed bracket and four new inserts (dropped into the holes by hand). Put the iron back in its stand with a heat-resistant glove if needed; the station stays on at 245 C. Seeds (HSI_SEED) set each insert's start height (4.2 to 4.8 mm proud) and the bracket's softness in the simulation.
fidelity: Approximate. PhysX cannot melt plastic: a rule moves each insert. It sinks only after 2.5 s of the iron pressing on it (pin within 1.5 mm of its axis), then at 0.3 mm/s per N above 1.5 N (bracket softness +-25% by seed). Over 15 N while sinking: forced; iron leaning over 5 deg while sinking: crooked; iron on the bracket 0.5 s: melt mark. Values are estimates from the insert makers' guidance (light steady push, a few s); README gives a kitchen-scale method to measure them. Bracket fixed in place.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (seed 0; also 1.0 on seeds 4 and 10)
